description:
'''UK underground rap''' (also referred to as '''UK underground''', '''UK UG''', or '''Overground''') is a [[UK rap]] [[Indie music scene|scene]] that emerged in [[London]] during the early 2020s. The scene differs from earlier waves of [[Underground hip-hop|underground]] UK hip-hop through its strong influence from [[Music of the United States|American]] [[internet rap]] genres such as [[cloud rap]], [[Plugg music|plugg]], [[Rage music|rage]] and [[Jerk (music genre)|jerk]]. 

Much like the [[Britpop]], [[Mod (subculture)|mod]] or [[Punk subculture|punk]] movements, the scene places [[British national identity|Britishness]] at the forefront, with many artists of foreign backgrounds, especially [[Black British people|Black British]] artists, reclaiming [[Union Jack|the Union Jack]] and [[Culture of the United Kingdom|British cultural imagery]] as an act of defiance against the [[Far-right politics in the United Kingdom|far-right]]'s [[Operation Raise the Colours|use of the Union Jack]]. Speaking with ''[[The Guardian]]'', director Lauzza added that young people were "creating our own Britain and our own culture that we can be proud of".

Notable artists associated with the scene include [[EsDeeKid]], [[Fakemink]], [[Rico Ace]], [[Fimiguerrero]], [[Feng (rapper)|Feng]], [[Lancey Foux]], [[Jim Legxacy]], and [[YT (rapper)|YT]]. The scene has achieved significant [[critic]]al and commercial success, and much like the name "[[Indie rock|indie]]" rock, the term "underground" is now often used to refer to the genre [[Musical style|stylistically]] rather than denoting popularity. The scene has been called "the UK's rap revolution".
